claims.text: Refractory high-entropy alloys can be used as structural materials for high-temperature plasma-facing components in fusion reactors.
Adding low-activation elements to refractory HEAs makes them suitable as low-activation structural materials.
W, V, and Ti are examples of low-activation elements suitable for this alloying strategy.
The proposed initial material is a polycrystalline refractory HEA.
The intervention is the addition of W, V, Ti, or other low-activation elements to refractory HEAs.
The intended service environment is the high-temperature, irradiated environment of a fusion reactor.
Adding the selected elements will produce an optimized alloy composition.
The addition of low-activation elements improves irradiation resistance.
The addition of low-activation elements improves high-temperature mechanical properties.
The modified refractory HEAs will exhibit enhanced low-activation properties.
The modified refractory HEAs will exhibit enhanced high-temperature resistance properties.
Traditional alloys have insufficient high-temperature mechanical properties or irradiation resistance for the intended application.
The approach is limited by the availability of low-activation elements.
The approach is limited by the compatibility of low-activation elements with refractory HEAs.
